headline_draft: Claude Code gets spellcheck, improved terminal UI, and bug fixes; signals continued focus on all-day developer and PM workflows
summary: Claude Code added optional spellcheck in the prompt input (using aspell, hunspell, or ispell), improved terminal UI readability and list rendering, fixed nested markdown list alignment, and boosted background cloud-session performance. The updates are small but targeted: reducing friction for all-day users. Combined with previous updates (auto-continue, subagent spawn cap removal), Claude Code is being shaped not as a demo tool but as everyday infrastructure for devs and PMs. Each update removes a friction point between thought and execution.
why_pm: If you ship features with Claude Code or Claude Cowork, these updates signal that Anthropic is optimizing for sustained daily use, not just impressive showcases. The spellcheck in the prompt, better terminal rendering, and reliability improvements all point to a tool designed to live in your workflow for hours at a time. This is a shift from 'AI as occasional accelerator' to 'AI as infrastructure.' PMs should test whether your teams are ready for that shift.
key_facts: Claude Code now includes optional spellcheck in prompt input
Improved terminal UI readability and list rendering
Fixed nested markdown list alignment at depth 3+
Boosted background cloud-session performance and VS Code reliability
Pattern: incremental friction reduction for all-day usage

headline_draft: Kredily KAI: Payroll and HR execution moves from chat to autonomous back-office agent
summary: Kredily announced Kredily 3.0 on August 14 and introduced KAI, an agentic AI system for payroll and HR execution. The company frames this as a move beyond conversational chat into high-compliance, mission-critical back-office work. KAI sits on top of Kredily's experience serving 25,000+ businesses and 1M+ employees, and the critical question is whether it can handle compliance-heavy tasks (taxes, deductions, regulations) well enough to earn trust from lean HR teams without requiring constant human oversight.
why_pm: This marks a category shift: AI agents are now shipping not as demos or customer-service chatbots, but as autonomous executors of high-consequence, compliance-heavy workflows. For HR, payroll, and finance PMs, this reframes the value prop from "faster chat" to "fewer errors + fewer headcount." The adoption bet rides on trust and error rates, not feature breadth.
key_facts: Kredily 3.0 launched August 14, 2026 with KAI as agentic execution layer
KAI targets payroll and HR execution—high-compliance, mission-critical workflows
Kredily serves 25,000+ businesses and 1M+ employees (scale signal)
Positioning as autonomous executor, not chat assistant or analytics tool
Key risk: whether end-to-end compliance execution can be trusted without constant human review
quotes: For those tracking agentic AI products, this signals a move beyond chat into back-office work that companies need done correctly every pay cycle. The key question is whether KAI can handle compliance-heavy tasks well enough to win trust from lean HR teams.
